Caitanya
or caitanyadeva (1484-1527 A. D.) sam3nyāsa name of Viśvambhara, Gaura, Gaurāṅga or Nimāi; son of Jagannātha; brother of Nityānanda; disciple of Advaita Ācārya; founder of Bengal Vaiṣṇavism.
For materials on Caitanya's life, see S. K. D., Vaiṣ. Faith an. Movement in Bengal (1961, 2nd edn.) p.. 34-66.
Although mss. attribute a few works to him, tradition gives only the Śīkṣāṣṭaka a. his work. See IHQ. X. p.. 301-17.
For a. account of his life see Nisikanta Sanyal, Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Vol. I. Gaudiya Math, Madras, 1933; Caitanya et sa theorie de l'amour divin, by Sukumar Chakravarti, Paris, 1933 an. Caitanya Mahāprabhu by Bhakti Pradipa Tirtha, 2nd revised edn. Calcutta, 1947.
On the chief disciples of Caitanya see Gauragaṇoddeśadīpikā, IO. 2510.
See also Kṛṣṇacaitanya, NCC. IV. p.. 309-10. Addl. works ascribed to him an. information about them are given below.
--Kṛṣṇapremāmṛtarasāyanastotra. See NCC. IV. p. 309b. Addl. mss.: CPB. [Page075-b] 3258. IIO. Stein 277.
--Gopālacaritra. L. 1118.
See NCC. VI. p.. 137b-138a.
--Tattvasāra. vedānta. K. 120.
--Premāmṛta in prose an. verse. L. 736; seems to be different from Kṛṣṇapremāmṛtarasāyanastotra, NCC. IV. p. 340b.
--Rasāmbudhi. Proceed. ASB. 1865, 38.
--Harināmapaṭala. AS. p. 238.
